The documents under `docs/` are written in Chinese; this README and the code comments are bilingual.
A **reverse-engineering mode** for **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)**.
It adds one entry to the dsh preset picker. Select it and the agent carries the reverse-engineering

tooling of REA (~139 tools over Ghidra / Hopper / IDA, binaries and
Electron artifacts), a reverse-e

ngineer persona, and an evidence-first analysis workflow skill — ready
to work on a sample straight

er persona, and an evidence-first analysis workflow skill — ready
to work on a sample straight away.
## What it does
- **Disassembly / decompilation** — Ghidra, Hopper and IDA through their headless or CLI entry point

s:
pseudocode, cross references, call graphs, function boundaries.
- **Binary reconnaissance** — str

ings, symbols, sections, import/export tables, entropy, compiler fingerprints.
- **Packaged artifact

s** — Electron `.app` and asar, APK / IPA, JS bundles: unpack, then analyse.
- **Cross-checking** —

the same function compared across engines, so one decompiler cannot mislead you.
- **Written finding
s** — notes written as evidence then conclusion, not as guesses.
A missing engine only removes its own group of tools; everything else keeps working.
## Why use it
| Advantage | Detail |
| One command | `npm run setup` installs into every surface, probes engines, verifies, then tells yo

u what to restart. |
| One bundle, four surfaces | Desktop app, `dsh web`, dsh-tui and headless shar

e the same bundle — no per-surface config. |
| Leaves the host alone | It only adds a subtree to a p

reset; permissions, model routing, sandbox and persistence stay yours. |
| Portable | No machine-spe

cific paths; engine locations come from environment variables. |
| Never resident | No engine at hos
t boot: the tool list comes from a local manifest, REA starts on the first real tool call and stops

itself after 10 idle minutes. |
| Fails softly | If REA cannot start, the mode is still selectable —

just without its tools. |
| Clean uninstall | Remove the bundle and you are back to stock; the ship

ped composition is untouched. |
| Self-checking | `npm run verify` checks structure and portability
offline; `verify:profiles` replays the real host loading path. |

### Per surface, manually
| You use | profile | Command | Takes effect |
| Desktop app | `desktop` | `dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:Verisw/rea-dsh` | Quit the app

fully (Cmd+Q), reopen |
| `dsh web` in a browser | `web` | `dsh plugin --profile web add github:Veri

sw/rea-dsh` | Restart `dsh web` |
| dsh-tui in a terminal | `dsh-tui` | `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tu

i add github:Verisw/rea-dsh` | Restart the TUI |
| `dsh -p` (scripts, headless) | `headless` | `dsh
plugin --profile headless add github:Verisw/rea-dsh` | Next run picks it up |
The desktop app and `dsh web` are separate profiles — installing into one affects only that surface.
The desktop profile must exist first (the app creates it), so quit the app before installing.

`dsh plugin` itself needs Node >= 22.18 / >= 24: earlier Node versions lack
`import.meta.main`, so t

he command exits 0 without doing anything. `npm run setup`
probes this; see docs/troubleshooting.md

A local checkout install also shows up in the plugin store (dsh-plugin-hub) under **your own plugins
**, where its publish button can push it to GitHub/npm. Being visible in the *public* store list is
a separate matter — see docs/market.md (zh).
## Use

1. Restart that surface.
2. `/preset` → **逆向工程模式** (reverse engineering), or `/preset reverse` direc

tly.
3. `/mcp` lists the `mcp__rea__*` tools; the engine itself starts on the first real call.
4. Po
int it at a sample and say what you want to know — behaviour, protocol, validation logic, version di
it at a sample and say what you want to know — behaviour, protocol, validation logic, version diffs.
Two things worth knowing:

- **A session with conversation history cannot switch presets** — start a new session.
- **The engin

e is not resident.** Mounting the mode starts a small supervisor only; the tool list is read
from a

local manifest (`~/.dsh/cache/dsh-rea-reverse-preset/`) so all 139 tools are still registered.
REA i

tself starts on the first real `mcp__rea__*` call (1–2 s warm) and stops after 10 idle minutes,
then

starts again on the next call.
A fresh machine has no manifest yet, so the first startup launches R

EA once to build it — or run
`npm run setup -- --warm` to do that up front, which also downloads the

ild it — or run
`npm run setup -- --warm` to do that up front, which also downloads the npx package.
### Engine locations (optional)

Nothing to configure: REA discovers engines itself. Use these when you have several versions or a

non-default location.
| Variable | Purpose |
| `HOPPER_LAUNCHER_PATH` | Hopper CLI launcher. On macOS the default location is used automatically

when present. |
| `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` | Ghidra install directory. The version must match what REA e

xpects (12.1.4 today). |
